title: Integral Laurent split-torus model, projection and coordinates
statement: Let $n\in\mathbf N$ and let $B$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Define the integral Laurent algebra $L_n=\mathbf Z[\mathbf Z^n]$, whose elements are finite sums $\sum_v a_v e^v$ for $v\in\mathbf Z^n$, with $e^v e^w=e^{v+w}$. Use the canonical universe lift of $\mathbf Z$ when needed. Give $L_n$ the Hopf structure $\Delta(e^v)=e^v\otimes e^v$, $\epsilon(e^v)=1$ and $\iota(e^v)=e^{-v}$. Define the integral split model $G_{n,\mathbf Z}$ to be its affine spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum], as a commutative group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ via this Hopf structure. Define $G_{n,B}$ to be its group-scheme base change [def-pc-base-change] along the unique $B\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Write $p_{n,B}:G_{n,B}\to\operatorname{Spec}L_n$ for the projection to the integral model. For $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, define its Laurent coordinate $x_i\in\Gamma(G_{n,B},\mathcal O)$ as the pullback along $p_{n,B}$ of the global section corresponding to $e^{\delta_i}\in L_n$, where $\delta_i$ is the $i$th standard basis vector. These constructions include $n=0$ with its empty coordinate family and impose no affineness, reducedness, connectedness or nonemptiness assumption on $B$.

source.place: Tag 022U, example-multiplicative-group: integral Laurent Hopf model and arbitrary base change; finite products. See also Milne, Algebraic Groups (2017), Examples 12.1--12.2 and Remark 12.6.
